This was a tough call. The amount of water in the gauge seemed pretty remarkable for just dew or fog, but weather radar archives show no clear signal of a rain shower overnight, just a lot of diffuse light and dark blue. The answers in FAQ about how to deal with gauge measurements potentially from dew or fog as a form of precipitation versus a form of air moisture don’t help me decide what to do because indicates that if the ground is moist we should count it as precipitation. But the ground was already moist from the prior several days of heavy rain we had, and this morning the grass and deck and stone features were wet. So I guess I’ll call it precipitation and leave my record as it, but I’ll let it be your call whether or not to include it. I also was not sure what times to put down, but according to whether radar, there was a lot of light and dark blue over our area overnight from about 9pm to 5:30 am. I couldn’t be sure it wasn’t also bird and invertebrates in the air (bird migration has certainly started and young birds are in the midst of dispersals) in addition to precip or moisture, but I’m guessing it was mostly heavy heavy fog or dew. Interestingly, however, there was no fog when I woke up this morning at about 630: the air was clear, which typically is not the case when we’ve had a big rain followed by a heavy fog overnight (it takes quite a while of sun shining to b urn it odd). So maybe there was a light drizzle precipitating out of a dew?
